properties.name: Big Bone Lick
properties.title: Big Bone Lick
properties.subtitle: Boone County / salt lick & fossil beds
properties.history: Big Bone Lick was a mineral spring where Pleistocene mastodons, mammoths, and ground sloths left bones in the mud while seeking salt. Native peoples and later explorers—including Christopher Gist—collected fossils here; Thomas Jefferson later studied specimens from the lick. The site became Big Bone Lick State Historic Site, one of Kentucky’s earliest windows on deep time and a waypoint for salt hunters on the Ohio frontier.

properties.name: Lexington Named
properties.title: Lexington Named
properties.subtitle: Fayette County / McConnell Springs
properties.history: In early June 1775, William McConnell’s surveyors camped on a sinking spring of Elkhorn Creek when word arrived of the April 19 fight at Lexington, Massachusetts. They named the camp for that battle and returned east; permanent settlement waited until 1779, when Robert Patterson’s party built a blockhouse near present Main and Mill. Virginia established the town in 1782—the springs chose the site, the Revolution chose the name.
